page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.d1ne-c14d3.14xlarge is a dedicated big data instance designed for massive local capacity and high data throughput. Powered by the x86_64 architecture on the KVM hypervisor, it features 56 dedicated vCPUs from an Intel Xeon E5-2682v4 processor clocked at 2.5 GHz. The system provides 160.0 GB of system memory, which allocates approximately 2.86 GB of RAM per vCPU, paired with a robust 35 Gbps baseline network bandwidth profile.

The primary differentiator of this instance is its massive bundled local storage configuration, comprising 70,866 GB of local mechanical hard disk drive (HDD) capacity. It operates without dedicated GPU acceleration. This architectural combination delivers an exceptionally high storage density per compute unit, designed specifically for sequential bulk I/O rather than low-latency random reads and writes.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, bundling tens of terabytes of local spinning disks provides economical large-scale storage per gigabyte compared to cloud-attached block volumes or solid-state alternatives. However, the architectural tradeoff relies on spinning media characteristics, which introduce latency penalties for random I/O operations and lack hardware-level cryptographic or modern vector extensions indicated in its CPU configuration.

Due to its high disk capacity, substantial vCPU allocation, and wide network pipe, the ecs.d1ne-c14d3.14xlarge is best matched with big data analytics processing, distributed Hadoop/HDFS data nodes, MapReduce pipelines, sequential log analysis, and large-scale data warehousing workloads.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.d1ne-c14d3.14xlarge is a big data cloud instance equipped with 56 dedicated Intel Xeon E5-2682v4 vCPUs running at 2.5 GHz on an x86_64 architecture. The system integrates 160.0 GB of system RAM, offering roughly 2.86 GB per core, complemented by a substantial 35 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. Its central feature is an integrated local storage array totaling 70,866 GB of HDD capacity, eliminating the need for attached network volumes for massive bulk datasets. Lacking discrete GPUs and utilizing mechanical disks rather than SSDs, it prioritizes sequential throughput and capacity density over microsecond random I/O latency. This hardware profile makes the instance particularly effective for large-scale distributed analytics engines, MapReduce jobs, HDFS data node architectures, and long-term sequential log processing clusters.
